newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Singleton mulls exit from TEN Network.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Singleton mulls exit from TEN Network.

text.p: John Singleton Advertising Ltd (JSA) said on Tuesday it had commissioned expert advice on a mechanism for selling down part or all of its 10 percent stake in unlisted television broadcaster TEN Group Ltd.

"The company is currently considering its options in respect of its investment in TEN and has commissioned expert advice on the mechanisms for, and benefits of, exiting whole or part of our holding in TEN for full value," JSA said in a statement accompanying its annual results.

JSA, floated in January 1994, comprises two wholly-owned subsidiaries, John Singleton Advertising (Aust) Pty Ltd, the largest wholly Australian owned advertising agency, and Belshaw Pty Ltd which holds the company's 10 percent stake in TEN.
The stake represents a five percent economic interest in TEN.
CanWest Global Communications Inc of Canada owns owns 15 percent of TEN but has a 57.5 percent economic interest.
JSA said that as part of the review it had reclassified its stake from a non-current asset to a current asset.
Managing director Russell Tate said a total of 18 new accounts were secured during the year. "Only one account of any significance was relinquished," he said.
"Advertising spend levels have been depressed in virtually all categories and particularly in the second half of 1995/96," Tate said.

"Most agencies are struggling to get close to prior year results," he said. "To have achieved our targets and significantly improved on the record results we set last year is quite an achievement in these market conditions," he said.

The company said it expected to get a dividend from TEN before the end of 1996 and that it would in turn pay a dividend to shareholders during this period which should exceed last year's unscheduled dividend of 10 cents a share.
JSA also reported a net profit of A$6.26 million for the year to June 30, up from A$5.84 million a year earlier.
Sales rose to A$20.67 million from A$18.27 million.
Final dividend was 10 cents a share for a total of 24 cents for the year, up from 23 cents a year earlier.
